Neutrophil activation accompanies neutrophil-predominant leukocytosis during Still disease flares; the edge is typed UNKNOWN because the cited clinical evidence does not resolve whether activation drives cell-number expansion or merely co-occurs with it.
Macrophage activation drives a T helper 1 (Th1) cell cytokine response.
Cytokine amplification contributes to the systemic hyperinflammatory state; organ-level intermediates are not represented in this compact pathograph.
Spiking fever is a defining manifestation of the systemic inflammatory state; intervening thermoregulatory mechanisms are not modeled.
Evanescent rash is a defining manifestation of systemic inflammation; its intervening skin-level mechanisms are not modeled.
Arthralgia and arthritis are defining manifestations of the systemic inflammatory state; synovial intermediates are not modeled.
Pharyngitis is clinically associated with AOSD, but the evidence does not establish a specific causal route from the systemic state.
Hepatomegaly is a reported multiorgan manifestation, but the organ-specific causal route is not established by the cited cohort.
Splenomegaly is a reported multiorgan manifestation, but the organ-specific causal route is not established by the cited cohort.
Pericarditis is a reported systemic manifestation, but the cited cohort does not establish the organ-specific causal route.
Myalgia is a reported systemic manifestation, but the cited cohort does not establish a muscle-specific causal route.
MAS is a severe hyperinflammatory complication of AOSD; the transition from ordinary disease activity to MAS remains incompletely resolved.
